# Pi adapter for the reviewed pstack source

The behavior source is the immutable `vendor/upstream/0.15.32/pstack/` Markdown snapshot at `99b609a72323b70204eab407c622f436e858e112`. The generated supported Skill/playbook entrypoints retain its instructions, with platform adaptations in a separate prelude. Do not summarize away upstream rules. The eleven core workflows retain critical-rule mappings; other generated entrypoints preserve the latest source without claiming full behavioral audit.

Apply user instructions and repository authority first. Apply the pinned upstream decision rules next, subject only to the explicit overrides below. Never run a Cursor command literally or assume a missing capability completed. Read referenced source Markdown through `pstack_skill` with `upstream/skills/<skill>/...` resource IDs; consume every page. Original relative links resolve within that snapshot. Markdown references are also installed alongside the generated Skills. Statechart scripts are bundled at skills/statechart/scripts; they require real Java/TLC and optional PNG renderer dependencies. Other plugin skills, private APIs, Cursor scripts, control drivers and cloud resources are not supplied. Report unavailable dependencies and their effect on the requested outcome.

## Platform substitutions

- Pi Skill frontmatter uses the resource directory name in lowercase kebab case. Upstream 0.15.32 already uses `poteto-mode`; bodies and manual invocation flags remain intact.

- Task and cloud workers map to `pstack_agents` and `pstack_workflow` Pi AgentSessions. The parent keeps playbook ownership. Parallel writers require separate Git worktrees; integrated delivery requires an explicit integrator followed by verification of the combined artifact. These are local processes, not cloud VMs.
- Map upstream reasoning effort to Pi `thinkingLevel` and choose an available `provider/model` for speed. With same-family fallback enabled, unsupported explicit levels use the nearest lower supported reasoning level and report the change; an unresolvable choice blocks. Cursor `-fast` aliases are not rewritten.
- Resolve model roles through `~/.pi/agent/pstack-native/models.json` (or PSTACK_NATIVE_HOME). Use `pstack_semantics` panel preflight. The optional same-family fallback chooses a registered available model from the same provider and a recognized family, reports substitutions, and otherwise blocks. It does not invent a family from a provider name or retry authentication/inference failures.
- `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, `.cursor/skills` and Cursor's plugin paths map to Pi configuration and the bundled snapshot. They are not files the Pi worker should create in a user's repository.
- Custom Mode maps to sticky `/poteto-mode`. `/loop` maps to `/pstack-loop`, which needs an active Pi host. Cloud-root hourly execution and exact delivery across a crash are unavailable; report this limitation before promising unattended audit coverage.
- Use a named available CLI/UI driver for real-surface proof. If no driver can reach the surface, return BLOCKED or inconclusive with the exact reason. Unit tests, fake providers, a worker's report or CI alone cannot replace the live lane.

## Explicit policy deviations

- For initial or major autopilot changes, require a full swarm. For a minor fix, rebase or conflict resolution, one fresh independent follow-up reviewer can replace a new full swarm only when a clean initial/major round is supplied. Fresh gates and live proof still run at the current head/base. A follow-up without that prior full round is blocked.
- Any head OR base change invalidates native verification and every round receipt, even when stable patch IDs match. Re-run lanes on the current exact pair. Upstream's build-noise/patch-ID reuse exception is intentionally disabled; the stricter native ledger policy remains in force.
- Read-only reviewer/verifier sessions inspect confined source and evidence; they cannot run shell commands. Deterministic commands run in the native verification runner or an authorized writable lane. A separate actor inspects the receipts; a writer cannot countersign its own work.
- Native arena and architect templates use one read-only cross-judge that inspects verified candidate worktrees through confined `pstack_candidates` tools. Candidate freshness is checked during judging and before integration. `judgeMode: per-candidate` retains the legacy template. Native specialized templates are mechanisms, not automatic completion of a named upstream playbook.
- Native swarm templates cover partition and best-of race. Mixed/first-pass/rank-all require an explicit DAG and declared selection policy; do not silently relabel best-of as first-pass.
- The native autopilot templates prepare local DAG artifacts. Full owner lifecycle, early ready PR, decisions.tsv/children.tsv, periodic audit, rebase discipline, root countersigns and stop propagation remain obligations of the coordinator. The stack template is not a delivered remote PR stack; use stack-plan/stack-open with correct parent worktrees.
- Babysit stops before merge, even when checks are green. Opening a PR does not start a babysit. An explicitly assigned full-autonomy owner may begin its assigned loop after its code-ready report; other agents finish their phase or stack before the handoff. Autopilot-stack stops before shipping. Full-autopilot still needs the operator's go; operator-reserved items never merge automatically. Use `pstack_semantics` round checks before a clean verdict, then native Frontier, ledger and authorization checks for any shipping operation. The round check neither attests the truth of supplied receipts nor authorizes a remote action.

## Unsupported operations

`Cursor-private-PR-provenance`, `Cursor-watch-READY`, `Cursor-cleanup-plugin` and `Bugbot-pass-dismissal` are unsupported. Querying one through `pstack_semantics` fails with an explicit error. GitHub/Origin state and native watch states are usable alternatives only within their own evidence boundary, not proof that a Cursor operation ran. Private provenance, queue verdicts and pass-based dismissal cannot be inferred from green CI. Do not mark a workflow complete when one of its required operations is unavailable.

## Evidence boundary

`SEMANTICS.json` records critical-rule mappings, exact source ranges, deviations, test references and review fingerprints. Inventory counts, mapping coverage, deterministic receipt tests, fake-provider Pi lifecycle tests and real-model runs are separate evidence levels. No mapping asserts complete chat/model equivalence. Updating a fingerprint records review work; it is not semantic approval. Advancing a source pin does not grant semantic approval; that still requires explicit maintainer sign-off. The active source is 0.15.32; its implementation audit, maintainer semantic sign-off and real-model evidence remain separate fields in SEMANTICS.json. The previous 0.15.17 snapshot is retained for provenance.

## Pinned upstream instructions

Source: cursor/plugins@99b609a72323b70204eab407c622f436e858e112, pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md. The following body is retained verbatim.

## Steps

### Multi-phase or multi-PR plan

**You own the plan, not the code. The plan is a checklist an owner runs box by box and the operator audits from the evidence.** The plan is the deliverable. Do not implement.

1. When the change is one or two files with an obvious approach, skip the plan. Say so and stop.
2. Settle open questions by prototype before you write. Run `playbooks/prototype.md` for each. Keep the branch, the SHA, and the screenshots for Appendix A. Ask the operator only about a product or preference call that no run can settle. Give options (the **never-block-on-the-human** principle skill).
3. Explore in subagents with `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"` and an explicit model per the Subagents section (the **guard-the-context-window** principle skill). Pick each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for the job, per the Subagents section. Each returns file pointers, conventions, test commands, and entry points. No inlined dumps.
4. Copy the skeleton below into the plan file and fill every placeholder. Unless the operator names a path, write the file under the agent store's `docs/`. Keep every heading and every sub-block in the order shown. One section per PR. One PR is one change with its own evidence (the **sequence-verifiable-units** principle skill). Name the execution playbook in **How to read this**. Pick between `playbooks/autopilot-full.md` and `playbooks/autopilot-stack.md` per the rule at the end of `playbooks/autopilot-stack.md`. A standing program takes `playbooks/orchestrate.md`.
5. Write under `/technical-writing` in full, then `/unslop`. The body is one Diátaxis mode, how-to. Appendices hold explanation and reference. Each heading states the task or the finding. No long dashes. No mid-sentence colons.
6. Run `node pstack/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/check-plan.mjs <plan.md>` and fix every line it prints (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).
7. Hand back. Post the plan path and the script's output, then stop. Execution starts on the operator's explicit go, under the execution playbook the plan names.

**Verification.** Tests alone are not sufficient verification. A PR is verified only when its unit, live, and perf boxes are all checked (the **prove-it-works** principle skill). That sentence is the verification rule. Every verification block opens with it. The live block is mandatory. Ten lanes at the PR head drive the real surface through its control skill, per the **swarm** skill, on the `swarm workers` model (default `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast`). Each lane is one box with a concrete scenario, the screenshot it saves, and its pass predicate. One lane is the **Regression lane against trunk.** It runs the same load-bearing scenario on trunk and head. If trunk does not have the feature, the lane records that fact and gates the behavior the diff adds plus the end state the user waits for instead of inventing a trunk result. The perf gate is dual-sided. Trunk and head must both produce the named metric. If trunk lacks the feature, also isolate the work the diff adds and set an absolute budget for that work plus the end-to-end state the user waits for. Do not claim a ratio between unlike scenarios. The perf block names the metric, the interleaved probe, the trunk baseline measured first, and the rule with the number that fails. A PR that changes an interaction is review-gated. The operator reviews it in chat with screenshots and a video before merge. A PR that changes no interaction writes `**Review gate.** None. <PR id> is not review-gated.` and no boxes under it.

**Control skill.** Pick it by surface. Browser, Electron, and web UIs use `control-ui` from `cursor-team-kit`. CLIs and TUIs use `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit`. Native mobile uses whatever simulator-driving skill the repo has. A PR that touches two surfaces gets lanes on both. A surface with no control skill is a risk in Appendix C, and its live block still names how each lane drives it.

## Pi execution tools

Use `pstack_agents` for one child and `pstack_workflow` / `pstack_graph` for an explicit DAG. Roles are `architect`, `worker`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, `synthesizer` and `integrator`. Parallel writers use isolated worktrees, then an integrator. A verifier directly depends on the artifact owner. Inspect workflow status on recovery; completed nodes are not replayed. Check remote state before retrying external effects. `pstack_worktrees` cleans only owned clean worktrees.
